note: Hand-curated. Detection is automated (Federal Register, agency and White House announcements, court dockets) but assigning a modelling effect is a judgement call, so entries arrive as pull requests with an empty effect for a maintainer to fill. See PLAN.md 8.1. Every entry carries verified_against and confidence; the app must not display an entry whose last_checked is stale.

travel_ban_partial.note: Proclamation 10998, partial restrictions, added to the above for a combined 39.

iv_pause_75.note: INCOMPLETE. The full 75-country list was not captured during research; only a partial sample is recorded. Do not use this list to tell an individual they are unaffected. Resolve before the event layer gates any user-facing claim.

events.title: Stricter public charge standard for adjustment of status
events.summary: DHS rescinds the December 2022 public charge rule and replaces it with stricter sub-regulatory guidance and broad adjudicator discretion. A new Form I-485 keyed to the standard is issued the same day. Benefits received before the effective date are assessed under the old rule.

modeling.note: Direction is adverse for approval rates and adjudication speed, magnitude unknown. Leave null rather than invent a number; it widens the §6.5 approval curve rather than shifting it.

events.title: Immigrant visa interviews paused worldwide
events.summary: The State Department paused immigrant visa interviews at every post while consular officers complete public charge training. Adjustment of status at USCIS is not affected.

modeling.note: Unused EMPLOYMENT numbers stranded this way are lost at year end, not recycled. Unused FAMILY numbers do raise the next year's employment limit. See PLAN.md 1.5.

events.title: EB-4 non-minister religious worker category sunsets
events.summary: H.R. 7148, signed 3 February 2026, extended the non-minister special immigrant religious worker program only through 30 September 2026. No enacted further extension was found.

events.title: Travel ban, Proclamation 10949
events.summary: Entry restrictions on nationals of nineteen countries. Applies to entry from abroad; it does not by itself stop an adjustment of status case filed inside the United States.

events.title: Travel ban expansion, Proclamation 10998
events.summary: Partial restrictions added for twenty further countries, bringing the combined total to thirty-nine.

events.title: USCIS adjudication pause for travel-ban nationals
events.summary: Paused adjustment of status, work permit and advance parole adjudications for nationals of the listed countries. Began December 2025 for nineteen countries, expanded 1 January 2026 to thirty-nine, and was vacated by the District of Rhode Island on 5 June 2026. The underlying entry bans were not disturbed.

events.title: Immigrant visa issuance pause, 75 countries
events.summary: The State Department paused immigrant visa issuance for nationals of seventy-five countries on public charge grounds. A federal court held it unlawful and it ended on 21 August 2026.

modeling.note: Demand suppressed by a country-specific pause does not evaporate. The Visa Office reallocated the numbers by advancing other countries' cutoffs, and the affected countries rebound afterwards.

events.title: H-1B $100,000 fee proclamation
events.summary: Proclamation 10973 of 19 September 2025 required an additional $100,000 payment with certain H-1B petitions. The District of Massachusetts vacated the implementing guidance on 8 June 2026 and the First Circuit denied the government a stay on 24 July 2026, so it has not been enforceable since. A further proclamation signed 18 September 2026, effective 21 September, purported to extend the payment through 21 September 2027; the Northern District of California enjoined that renewal in part on 30 September 2026. Twice blocked, never in force for a full cycle. Affects the multi-year pipeline feeding future priority dates, not any current queue position.

modeling.note: The multiplier is conditional and currently dormant: the payment has been enjoined or vacated for all but a few weeks since first issued, so it has not yet suppressed a full filing cycle. Status keeps it out of isLive(), which is correct -- an unenforceable fee is not a live lever. Revisit if an appeal reinstates it, and note the renewal runs only to 21 September 2027 even if it does.

events.title: Wage-weighted H-1B selection
events.summary: Cap-subject H-1B registrations are selected with weighting by wage level. Registrations fell from about 344,000 to about 210,000 year on year, which reduces the pipeline feeding priority dates several years out.

events.title: Executive Order 14431, H-1B program integrity
events.summary: Signed 18 September 2026. Directs State, Labor and Homeland Security to weigh whether an H-1B sponsor has made layoffs in the previous year or plans them, to consult Commerce, Education and the Small Business Administration on wage and employment data when processing petitions and labour condition applications, and gives the Wage and Hour Division 30 days to begin reviewing past labour condition applications for action under INA 212(n)(2)(G).

modeling.note: Direction is adverse for H-1B inflow, magnitude unknown, so no multiplier. Nothing published says how many petitions the added scrutiny will stop, and that count is the entire effect size. Reaches a current queue position nowhere: it is about petitions and labour condition applications for workers entering, so like the other H-1B entries it touches the pipeline feeding priority dates years out.
modeling.not_the_perm_authority: Section 3(b) directs review of LABOUR CONDITION APPLICATIONS under INA 212(n)(2)(G), which is H-1B wage-and-hour enforcement. The suspension of eight employers from PERM is 20 CFR 656.31(b), a different programme under a different authority, so this order is NOT the primary source for dol-perm-suspension-eight-employers-2026 and must not be cited as one. The 30-day deadline here fell on 18 October and that suspension came on 8 October, which places them in the same enforcement wave, but nothing published states a causal link and this entry does not assert one.

events.title: Gold Card draws on EB-1 and EB-2 numbers
events.summary: A pay-for-priority route drawing visa numbers from the existing EB-1 and EB-2 pools without changing the statutory caps. Uptake has been negligible: a few hundred requests and one approval by mid-2026, with litigation pending.

modeling.note: Negligible at observed uptake. Revisit if approvals reach the thousands.

events.title: Per-country cap reform: EAGLE Act and IVES Act (118th Congress)
events.summary: S.3291 and H.R.6542, which would have phased out the seven percent per-country limit for employment-based green cards. Died with the 118th Congress on 3 January 2025 without passing either chamber. A bill does not carry over between Congresses; reintroduction under new bill numbers would need its own entry once one is confirmed, not a revival of this one.

modeling.note: Structural. Would be modelled as a scenario in Level C, not applied to the base estimate. Kept in the registry, not deleted, so the card's exclusion logic has a real dead entry to be tested against.

events.title: PERM suspended for eight large employers
events.summary: The Labor Department suspended Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini from the PERM labour certification programme on 8 October 2026, under 20 CFR 656.31(b), pending investigations into possible fraud or wilful misrepresentation. Pending applications are not processed and new ones are refused. An initial suspension runs up to 180 days and can be extended while an investigation continues. H-1B is not suspended, PERM is open to every other employer, and approved I-140s are not cancelled.

modeling.note: Direction is clear, size is not, so no multiplier. NOT future_demand: changing employer on an H-1B needs a fresh PERM and I-140 from the new employer and only the priority date carries over, so someone at one of these eight who is mid-PERM cannot file I-485 even once their date is current, the earlier I-140 having stopped being able to support a filing when they left that job. That is demand held back at the FRONT of the queue now rather than inflow years out, and the Visa Office advances cutoffs when annual numbers go unused. No number because nothing public says how many people at these eight are in that position, which is the entire effect size. It is a suspension and not a cancellation, so those cases return when it lifts and could retrograde dates later: the sign changes over time. Litigation at this scale is likely and would reverse it outright.
modeling.primary_source_note: Announced 8 October 2026 at a press conference by the Vice President and the Secretary of Labor. It is not a Federal Register document and, as of 12 October, has not appeared on OFLC's own announcements page, whose latest item is 17 September. verified_against stays null until an official notice exists to point at.
